name: CUTLASS / CuTe
production_evidence: TensorRT-LLM uses CUTLASS kernels for GEMM and attention
vLLM uses CUTLASS for some fused kernels
PyTorch uses CUTLASS for some GEMM operations
strengths: Highest performance: CUTLASS achieves the best known performance for GEMM on NVIDIA GPUs
Mature: nearly a decade of development, extensive architecture support (Volta through Blackwell)
Composable: hierarchical decomposition allows mixing and matching tiling strategies
CuTe DSL (CUTLASS 4.0+): Python interface that provides CUTLASS-level performance with a smoother learning curve
Extensive examples: 50+ example kernels covering GEMM, convolution, attention, and more
weaknesses: Very steep learning curve: C++ template metaprogramming is one of the hardest paradigms in systems programming
Long compile times: template instantiation can take minutes for complex kernels
NVIDIA-only: no AMD, Intel, or other GPU support
CuTe DSL is still in beta (as of CUTLASS 4.8, Sept 2026): not yet production-ready
Debugging is extremely difficult: template errors produce thousands-line error messages
No autotuning: tile sizes and other parameters must be chosen manually
notes: CUTLASS is NVIDIA's C++ template library for high-performance GEMM and related computations. It provides abstractions for hierarchical decomposition (thread block, warp, and thread-level tiling) and data movement (async copy, tensor core MMA). CUTLASS has been the foundation for nearly all high-performance NVIDIA GPU kernels since Volta. The learning curve is extremely steep: C++ template metaprogramming requires understanding of partial specialization, SFINAE, and complex type computations. Compile times are significant: a single complex kernel can take minutes to compile due to template instantiation. CUTLASS 4.0 introduced CuTe, a Python DSL that provides the same abstractions with a smoother learning curve and faster compile times. CuTe DSL is in public beta (as of 4.8, Sept 2026) and is expected to graduate by end of summer 2026. For production inference, CUTLASS is used indirectly through TensorRT-LLM and vLLM rather than directly by most teams. The realistic learning curve for CUTLASS C++ is 3-6 months to become productive; for CuTe DSL, 2-4 weeks.
